angles.drive: You wait your turn even when the turn is plainly yours to take. Going ahead of others feels like taking what nobody has offered you, and you stand back until someone calls your name. People with less to offer get there first.
angles.cost_self: Waiting your turn has kept you in the same seat for years. Being called forward matters more to you than stepping forward, and the call keeps going to louder people. Underneath, you want someone to see that you were ready long ago.
angles.cost_others: In meetings you wait your turn to speak, and the idea waits with you. Speaking before others feels like a step above your place, and the talk moves on before your turn comes. Your team loses the idea that would have helped them.

angles.drive: You stand by people through the lean years as well as the good ones. Being someone others can count on matters more to you than being exciting, and you stay when staying is dull. Old friends still call you first.
angles.cost_self: Standing by people means staying through their worst stretches. You need a bond to last more than you need it to be easy, and you keep showing up long after it stops being returned. Some years your loyalty costs you more than it brings back.
angles.cost_others: You stand by the people you have had for years. You need the old ties to stay strong, and newer faces take a long time to get in. Those who arrive late find a warm circle that is already full.

angles.drive: You ask why before you accept how things are done. An answer only feels like yours once you have pulled it apart, and you question the accepted way rather than take it on trust. Your questions turn up the flaw everyone else walked past.
angles.cost_self: Asking why keeps you from settling into any easy answer. You need to see the reason for yourself, and the comfort of simply believing stays out of reach. Each clear answer is paid for with some of your peace.
angles.cost_others: With other people's plans, you ask why before you join in. Taking part only feels honest once the reason holds up for you, and your questions arrive before your help does. Friends get a sharper plan and a slower yes.

angles.drive: You are open-handed the moment something good comes in. A gain only feels real to you once it has reached other people, and you pass part of it on the same day. Friends in a tight month find your hand already open.
angles.cost_self: Your open hand works in bursts, wide one month and closed the next. Giving has to feel alive to you rather than planned, and the bursts seldom match what you have spare. Some months your own plans go without.
angles.cost_others: The people near you get your open hand in bursts rather than a steady flow. You need a gift to come from the moment, and nobody knows when the next one is due. Those who rely on you plan around the good weeks.

angles.drive: You stay close to home and the few people who hold you steady. Being held is where you feel most yourself, and you go back to that shelter over any open road. The wider world reaches you mostly second-hand.
angles.cost_self: Staying close to home keeps you among people who already know you. You learn best where you feel held, and unfamiliar ground makes your mind go quiet. You miss what only a strange place would have shown you.
angles.cost_others: Staying close to home means the people near you go out without you. You need familiar walls around you to feel held, and the trips and evenings out happen in your absence. Those you love come home with stories you were not part of.

angles.drive: You hold back your yes until you are sure you will keep it. A promise you might break feels worse to you than none at all, and every offer waits while you check. Good offers run out in the gap.
angles.cost_self: Holding the yes keeps you out of promises you could not keep. You need your word to be solid before it leaves you, and a maybe can sit with you for weeks. Those weeks of maybe tire you more than the promise would.
angles.cost_others: The people who ask you for something wait longer for your yes than for anyone else's. Your yes has to be one you will stand behind, and the question hangs open while you weigh it. Their plans stay on hold until your answer comes.

angles.drive: You run a tight ship at home as well as at work. Loose ends feel like danger to you, and you keep every plan and every person on schedule. Home runs like clockwork and feels a little like a workplace.
angles.cost_self: Running a tight ship makes every small slip your problem. You need things under control to feel steady, and a late bus or a lost key sets your jaw. You use up your nerve on things that never needed it.
angles.cost_others: In your tight ship everyone has a job, and the people at home get theirs from you. You need the household to run like a team, and your requests land as orders. Your family does what you ask and keeps its ideas quiet.

angles.drive: You make things slowly and enjoy every stage. The pleasure of the making matters more to you than the finish line, and you never feel any need to rush. What you make carries that ease, and people sense it.
angles.cost_self: Being unhurried means your work takes the time it takes. Enjoying the making matters more to you than the deadline, and faster hands get their work out first. Some of the credit goes to them.
angles.cost_others: People waiting on something you are making get it in your own good time. You need the making to stay a pleasure, and you will not rush it for anyone's calendar. What arrives is worth having and a little late.

angles.drive: You keep to yourself even among people you like. Your own company is where you feel steady, and you share your days without sharing much of what is in them. Those who love you know your habits better than your heart.
angles.cost_self: Keeping to yourself spares you the work of explaining. You need your inner life to stay your own, and most of what you feel never gets said aloud. Underneath, you would like one person to know you well.
angles.cost_others: Keeping to yourself leaves the people close to you guessing at your mood. Privacy feels like solid ground to you, and your inner weather stays behind a quiet face. They are left to read you from small signs.

angles.drive: You love the craft for its own sake, whatever the thing you are making. Shaping something with care is where you feel most at home, and the hours pass without your counting them. What you make shows that it was enjoyed in the making.
angles.cost_self: Loving the craft draws you back to the work above almost anything else. You need part of every day to go into making something, and other plans wait their turn. Friends and sleep get whatever evenings the craft leaves over.
angles.cost_others: The people around you often find you deep in a piece of work. Losing yourself in the making is your favourite way to be, and a question from the doorway takes a moment to reach you. Your family shares you with the craft.

angles.drive: You wait to be told before you trust your own read. A word from someone wiser feels like cover, and you keep asking long after you know. You hand your best judgement to people who know less than you do.
angles.cost_self: Waiting to be told leaves your own good sense unused for weeks. You need someone above you to say it is safe, and their word comes later than your own read did. Your first instinct is often right and seldom acted on.
angles.cost_others: When others look to you for a call, you wait to be told too. You want the shelter of a wiser word first, and the people counting on you wait while you ask. They lose days to a decision you had already reached.

texts.text: Whenever someone arrives shaken, you offer them the shelter you would want for yourself. Firm ground is what you seek in a bad hour, and you hand on the words that once held you. Your warmth reaches them a step behind your advice.

You over-protect the people you love from what they could survive. Feeling safe is what you want most, and you hold them the way you wish to be held. Remember that you love them just as much when you let them struggle.
